newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-KARLSRUHE, 1860 BATTLE FOR UEFA CUP SLOT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KARLSRUHE, 1860 BATTLE FOR UEFA CUP SLOT.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund's European Cup triumph over Juventus was good news for their Bundesliga rivals.
The victory kept Dortmund in the tournament next season and created an extra UEFA Cup berth in Germany, adding some much-needed tension to Saturday's last day of the campaign.

Bayern Munich have already secured the championship while Leverkusen have made sure of second spot and the other European Cup place. At the other end of the table, Fortuna Duesseldorf, Freiburg and St Pauli have been relegated.
That puts the focus firmly on the battle between 1860 Munich and Karlsruhe for sixth place which -- thanks to Dortmund's win -- is now enough to automatically qualify for the UEFA Cup.
"I never doubted Dortmund would win the Champions' League final and we would then sort things out on the last day of the season," said 1860 coach Werner Lorant said.

The advantage lies with Lorant's side, who currently occupy sixth slot. A win over Werder Bremen would herald a long-awaited return to European competition for the club which for so long has languished in the shadow of city rivals Bayern.
But 1860 will have to survive without their brilliant playmaker Peter Nowak, who will be running the Polish midfield against England in a World Cup qualifier on Saturday.

"Normally if a player is missing, I don't give it a second thought," Lorant said. "But I can't understand this case, where an international match is taking place when there are still league games to be played in important countries."
Karlsruhe, just a point behind 1860 and with a superior goal difference, take on Freiburg.
"Everything's still possible," Karlsruhe captain Thomas Haessler said. "We have to win and Bremen have to help us."
Even if Haessler and his team mates fail to make sixth spot, their current seventh place may also be enough to ensure qualification.
If VfB Stuttgart beat regional league side Energie Cottbus in the German Cup final next month, they will enter the European Cup Winners' Cup and free up another UEFA berth.
But Karlsruhe president Roland Schmider wants his club to give 100 percent and not rely on others.
"We have to give everything and win in Freiburg so we can't blame ourselves at the end of the day," he said.
